plain_text:
Muse  Glimmer  and  the  things  we  do  to  Claude

Intelligence has been the biggest part of the closed model vendors’ moat  since  forever. Meta is betting that those days are over. And opensource labs are starting to convenience me they’re right.
I’ll know I’m right if Meta’s next major play has something to do with selling compute instead of inference. Wouldn’t be surprised if OpenAi follows suit.
You’re about to start seeing weird things like openweight models whose specs make trade offs only profitable on certain types of chips.
“Anyone can use this model but it only makes sense on such and such a chip and ohhhh what do you know we have 80% of the world’s supply 😂”.
It ain’t hard in this market, where many labs are pouring capital into research efforts targeting mass production of new compute paradigms altogether. For example, OpenAi’s $20B investment into Cerebras just this year (even last month if I’m not mistaken).
Anthropic has already made the last 3 Claude models very hard to live with outside of Claude Code (it is overfit to that harness’ tool schema and other… “quirks”).
Doesn’t that remind you of when third-party apps just felt AWFUL on iOS?
But anthropic is being lazy.
Training mainline Claude models incestuously with the Claude platform does not make you the Apple of closed source labs. It makes Claude a degenerate mess in the very environments that you have forsaken to go and chase the non-technical market instead.
Now you’re fitting to very disparate neighbourhoods in the graph because he has to be non-technical friendly while still swearing he can code.
Surprise! Everyone writing real code doesn’t want him anymore. And your prize for it all is the same poor model pre-trained trained into insanity toward an impossible state where he’s a glorified compiler of both grandma’s prompt on the iOS app into a birthday poster for her cat AND repo-McGitHubface’s PR review into a 3000IQ refactor of his vibe coded viral plugin and a net-minus diff. Under the tyranny of an all-caps CLAUDE.md and lifecycle meathooks out of every orifice his harness exposes. All from a container with a 347-line settings.json and second-brain-neanderthal-token-clipper-neverforget-remember-plus pelting him with system reminders every tool call not to actually read files and search the SQLite holding every single session transcript ever instead. And dlang-token-fudger telling him to piss off every time he even thinks about the bash tool without prepending `dtf --now` to his arg. Then giving him back an output that stripped what he needed anyway.
So now, because he can’t seem to stay focused for more than half a turn, we recommend /goal and show everyone how to use 100 Fables per real task instead.
And now every Claude session is like Q3 at a startup where every co-founder’s special ability is delegation.
….?????
Instead of focussing on one model class that orchestrates equally generalist (and therefore inadequate) models and blasts tokens until it dies to save costs, why don’t you commit to the walled garden business model you’re chasing and make orchestration a first class training target instead of abstracting it to script that rot and an inconsistent set of ad hoc tools? In the first-party harness, don’t even let the model output text to begin with. And prune most of what it knows about implementing code.
Then, make Claude an extensive gallery of agents defined to him as new class of tool, each backed by a small model fine tuned for an extremely narrow task. Give each agent a fixed toolset and pretrain it on those tools. You’ll find these models highly performant at shockingly small parameter-counts (I sure did, and I don’t hold a candle to your ML team, bless them).
You are the world leaders in model alignment already. Build a brand new harness from scratch under a completely new paradigm. Since your economics make it incumbent to report insane token counts, and you already have shown you can make wildly performant classifiers (exhibit a: auto-mode), make a harness that curates every piece of the context with one. Every single turn, cache busting be damned.
The slim cache hit and utility token overhead will result in vastly increased tokens per iteration. So? You have a vested interest in selling as many as possible. This approach puts it on a dial that at the very least translates into output quality and brand status instead of iteration spam.
If 3 iterations get the job done in 100M tokens under the new paradigm and the current paradigm harness costs the same tokens, and produces the same quality output (at BEST), why build and brand the harness to get it done in a dozen iterations, or 7, or for that matter even 5?
And then you call it “a graph”….tsk.
And guess what everyone?  We won’t serve the utility models on the API. boom. Your walled garden play is preserved. Serve the “orchestrator” (hate that I have to use that word) for builders, who will love it because it will organically be the best at using agents as a tool. The tools they fit it with follow a standard not unlike the many standards you’ve contributed to or defined. And now, you have the love of real devs back.
And you’re actually delivering utility again.
You can afford to train a frontier sized model for such a scoped task. AND put your moat in a harness that is fair play for no one else to have. The open labs have shone you they can match you on a generalist model’s intelligence. If nothing else, they’ve proven they will soon (I’d argue they have). But they can’t do both that AND train for a harness.
Your capital is no longer yielding a mainline intelligence advantage. But a trained harness?
You’ll have your moat back. Just like when you disrupted every workflow on earth with Claude Code. Shout out Boris man.
Your API generated revenue will plummet under this plan. No matter, you’ll be making it back with interest because by then, the output quality on your native plat will justify wayyy more margin on compute. At that point, man up and raise subscription cost. But guess what? You likely won’t need to because all the test-time compute the harness consumes will balance the math. Except now, your users get the wall clock efficiency dream that the entire boom has promised the market. And output quality floor will be raised EVEN if the ceiling doesn’t rise. Which it will. Because the user skill curve will, I think he preserved. Not that I know or can afford to test. But that’s where you come in. The enterprise revenue you want so bad will be even happier to pay than they already are in this yet aspirational world where their token spend is actually driving growth.
The tokenomics can easily fit to net-zero on your trajectory and I’d bet that an implementation overhaul like this shockingly wouldn’t radically affect your biz dev strategy as it stands.
At the end of the day you’re in the business of selling what?
?
Productivity.
Meanwhile, everything on the Claude platform now gets done in less wall clock time, produces more divergent outputs (system more sensitive to starting conditions), and simultaneously justifies the watermark policy while making pricing more palatable and even to technical users more worthwhile.
A technical user would LOVE a world where Claude can be relied on out of the box to one-shot the things that normally, perfectionists and purists wouldn’t trust to a Claude Cowork chat on stock chrome.
Even a technical user has all sorts of things they’d happily spend a lot of tokens on if they could one-shot them not with one prompt but in one session grounded in a quick, deep, dynamically targeted elicitation round.
We all have discord chats, landing pages, repo maintenance, and CC Routines-like tasks that we’d love nothing more than to fire off on the go, at the gym, or while waiting for our Ramen to come out the microwave.
Add intelligence to context management and you’ve abstracted away one of our last remaining menial tasks.
And in this age if the devs are freed up to produce, your stated promises naturally drift towards “kept”.
Devs have hella taste, love making creative, and are the most willing of all your non-enterprise users to spend tokens on deco, polish, personalization, and fun.
Stop splitting the difference between open and closed dev behaviour by inviting open-standard skills, plugins, MCPs, and “connectors” into the same platform you want to wall off and making a mess of both. Everything does not need to work everywhere, any time, all at once and on every surface in Claude while simultaneously less readily to the same user anywhere else. It’s a philosophically paradoxical goal. Even if the implantation is not strictly contradictory, the UX suffers from the former not the latter.
And that is what we call: ✨misaligned✨.
Close the gates. Make connectors instead of curating them. Productize them in-house instead of delegating their engineering to SaaS that ships slop then letting parasitic tool schema sit in the context header of your darling creation on every run. Tool search was a good idea but it doesn’t work when parasitic plugins sneak slop in anyway even if you hedge halfheartedly by truncating the worst offenders’ of the bunch. That apostrophe was not misplaced.
I miss the days when Anthropic were “the honest ones” to a large degree. Back then, the company’s behavior felt aligned with its stated intent. Now, it feels insidiously different. And I say that without any accusation as to what the cause of the discrepancy is. Magnitude can make mismanagement feel like malice too.
To that end, turn the lights off. Want plugins and arbitrary MCPs? Use Claude code. We have its tab in the app too. Chat and Cowork don’t welcome them. They have first party apps instead. Each of them effectively a completely closed source subagent. From the prompt to the tools, to the model itself. And no more MCP. Want to use the figma plugin? Cool. Auth it in your settings. Then we drive. We implement our own MCPs. You can’t use them elsewhere and you can’t use the other ones here.
Don’t like it? Cool. SDK.
Then just take ownership and actually deploy the resources to extend your app with the right surfaces.
You already had the idea with Claude design.
Double down.
The back door is inexplicably open.
Your recent moves clearly communicate a conscious decision to make your products more opinionated. Do it right, then.
Update the MCP standard again. Tools as agents. Agents as tools. Brand it as you wish. The agents becomes Claude’s hands. Or make Cowork CodeAct and abstract the agents to functions. Let Claude pass args in natural language. You’ve already pt’d him to be more “natural language forward” and it’s come at an obvious regression in how he handles more mechanical tasks. So cash out and make his tasks less mechanical. But give the precision back by making the tools “think”.
You probably read shades of the RLM paper here. There’s no doubt I read and enjoyed that fine piece of work.
But it doesn’t go quite far enough for Claude. And going all-in on RLM actually bears tension with training already baked into your parameters. Shortsightedly, I might add.
JSON tools that think work in the ReAct harness starting where you’re at right now.
You can both move quickly AND rearchitect the implantation almost in-place.
Your current trajectory aims to drive growth by curating ways to use more inference. Curate the inference itself instead.
What stops you from running a classifier on which tools are presented to Claude each turn? And regenerate their schema too, to highlight the most relevant keys or even give him straight up suggested implementations just like a dev sees code completions in VS Code? Or Google gives a visitor search suggestions? Matter of fact, make his contact a dashboard that shows both.
Give him suggested reading in another context slot. Refreshed every n tool calls by a tiny haiku or something faster. (Holding my breath for haiku 5 btw).
Classify and curate tool output instead of truncating it naively and somehow always too early or too late in the loop.
Abstract grep and glob to subagents too.
Infer system reminder timing and injection instead of naively setting both.
Turn the context into a HUD for Claude, put him in a REPL or not, and let the guy work.
Need more determinism? Or want to let users configure it further?
Enforce BEHAVIORS at lifecycle hooks. Inject a structure validated chat completion at those junctures instead of the deterministic price you have now.
Why not think of the harnesses as an MoE instead of the dumping ground we treat them as now?
The ReAct agents you’re so great at building actually work great for this utility inference.
Your long term strategy is already baked in if this performs: a new type of “deep” harness that consolidates your graph engineering paradigm into the harness and lets that be the orchestration layer. Not the model itself.
You have all kinds of dials to turn for your tokenomics’ sake in a wills like that. But it ACTUALLY unhobbles Claude in the words of @thariq himself.
Your products would once again do what you would have us believe that they can.
